title: BeforeShare inspection result
description: The canonical result of one inspection run. The desktop application, the CLI and the local MCP server all return this exact structure (§14.1); none of them may add, drop or reinterpret a field.

schemaVersion.description: MAJOR.MINOR. See docs/contracts/inspection-result.md for what counts as a breaking change. Compatibility policy is finalised by issue #25.

path.description: Absolute, fully resolved path - symlinks resolved before access (§13.4). Present here because the caller supplied it and needs to know which file was read. §21.2 forbids paths in LOGS and exported diagnostics; it does not forbid them in the result returned to the caller. Anything that persists or forwards this result is responsible for stripping it.

mediaType.description: Determined by content sniffing, never by file extension. This is the type that was actually inspected.

declaredMediaType.description: The type the filename extension claimed, present ONLY when it disagrees with mediaType. A disagreement also raises a media_type_mismatch limitation - it is never resolved silently.

coverage.description: What was actually checked. §17.1 requires 100% accurate coverage reporting and 0 checks mislabelled as completed, so skipped and failed entries carry a reason rather than being bare identifiers: a detector that did not run must say why it did not run.

findings.description: Ordered deterministically: severity descending (critical, high, medium, low), then category ascending, then the canonical serialisation of location ascending, then id ascending. The order is part of the contract because §17.5 requires byte-identical output for repeated inspection of the same file at the same detector versions.

limitations.description: What narrows the meaning of this result. A limitation is not a warning banner: each one names the detectors it affected, which is what prevents `no_findings` from being emitted while a suppressed check goes unmentioned (§5.8).

versions.description: Which code produced this result (§14.1). Granularity and the compatibility policy around it are finalised by issue #25; the shape is fixed here because every example and every test needs it.

cancelled.description: True when the run ended because the user cancelled. A cancelled run is never `no_findings`; it is `partial` or `failed` per the rules in issue #18.
